Verdict: request changes. The author is trying to ensure every generated Gradle VERIFY command tests the edited project. The PR improves several paths, but that guarantee still has a hole.

Short answer to your scope question: only computed includes are reasonably out of scope. Nested builds and the misleading fallback are deferred work, not outside the problem described by [issue #219](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/issues/219).

## Spec

**Act on**

- High: A rejected child project can still fall through to an included non-root parent. [deriveSearchVerifyCommand](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/entire-graph/fix-gradle-verify-project-membership-219/internal/sem/search_verify.go:514) continues walking after [deriveSearchVerifyGradle](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/entire-graph/fix-gradle-verify-project-membership-219/internal/sem/search_verify.go:2021) rejects the child.

  Concrete case:

  ```text
  settings.gradle          includes :parent
  parent/build.gradle
  parent/child/build.gradle
  parent/child/src/main/java/A.java
  parent/child/src/test/java/ATest.java
  ```

  `:parent:child` is correctly rejected, but the walk then emits:

  ```sh
  ./gradlew :parent:test --tests 'ATest'
  ```

  That command does not establish coverage of `parent/child`. This contradicts the PR’s central claim that fallback stops at an unproven Gradle boundary.

- Medium: The repaired rejection path still reports “no build manifest found” through [searchVerifyNoneCommand](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/entire-graph/fix-gradle-verify-project-membership-219/internal/sem/search_verify.go:91). The existing [test fixture](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/entire-graph/fix-gradle-verify-project-membership-219/internal/sem/search_verify_gradle_membership_test.go:33) contains `lib/build.gradle`, and the verbose test confirms the false message. This should say that no safe command could be derived.

**Consider**

- Independent nested-build support belongs to #219. The issue says a directory with its own settings “is a separate build root” and notes that narrow verification lacks a `-p` form. A partial PR may defer that command shape and use `Refs #219`, as [PR #249](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/249) does, but it cannot treat the issue as finished.

**Noted**

- Computed includes may safely remain unsupported at [searchVerifyGradleSettingsIncludes](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/entire-graph/fix-gradle-verify-project-membership-219/internal/sem/search_verify.go:767). Proving arbitrary Groovy or Kotlin configuration would require executing repository data or building an unsound partial evaluator. Conservative refusal matches the safety contract.

**Dismissed**

- Requiring support for every dynamic settings program. The correct static answer for unprovable membership is no command.

Worst spec issue: the PR still permits an ancestor command that may not test the edited child project.

## Standards

**Act on**

- Gradle ownership policy is split across the narrow walker, suite walker, and root-only guard. That structure caused the missed non-root fallback. The fix should give derivation a way to distinguish “no match here, keep walking” from “this is a Gradle boundary, stop.” Add the included-parent/undeclared-child regression through `buildSearchVerifyCommand`.

- Treat the residual state as unresolved, not absent. Change the generic fallback wording and assert the full output, not only `Tier == "none"`.

**Consider**

- The tests check generated strings but never launch Gradle. One small real-Gradle fixture would anchor the `-p` and project-path assumptions to the external tool’s behavior.

**Noted**

- `mise run check` passed fully in 573.72 seconds, including formatting, vet, build, 164 status-line checks, and the race-enabled suite.
- The focused Gradle family passed.
- No measurable performance regression appeared: 1,000 repetitions took 1.332s on the branch versus 2.079s on upstream main. Repository reads remain capped at 256 paths.
- The review made no changes. `HANDOFF.md` remains untracked.

**Dismissed**

- File size alone is not a new blocker. `search_verify.go` grew from 3,050 to 3,105 lines and was already beyond the threshold.
- A nested directory that is both included by root settings and has its own settings is not automatically a correctness failure. The root project may legitimately use the same directory. That needs a real Gradle counterexample before becoming a blocker.

**Draft GitHub review**

> Request changes
>
> The root and suite cases are improved, but the narrow walk can still escape a rejected Gradle boundary.
>
> If root settings include `:parent`, while `parent/child` has its own undeclared `build.gradle`, rejecting `:parent:child` does not stop `deriveSearchVerifyCommand`. It walks to `parent` and emits `./gradlew :parent:test --tests 'ATest'`, which does not establish coverage of the edited child.
>
> Please add a production-seam regression for that layout and make a declined Gradle boundary stop narrow ancestor discovery.
>
> The residual result also says “no build manifest found” for fixtures that contain `lib/build.gradle`. Please use a reason that describes the actual state, such as “no safe verification command derivable,” and assert that output in the rejection test.
